steps.line: Hi Isla, thanks for seeing her today. She was pretty quiet in the car on the way home, though honestly she's usually quiet after school lately. Anyway, we'll see you next Thursday.

Hi Isla, just wanted to let you know she asked me to leave the hallway light on tonight instead of turning every switch off like she usually does. And she put her notebook on the kitchen table for me to see. Thank you for today.

She hummed the whole way home in the car. It's that old song her dad and I used to play on Friday nights, and I haven't heard her hum it since the spring. I didn't say a word because I didn't want her to stop. Thank you, Isla.

We just got in from the bus. Leo chattered the whole ride about his frog hospital, and then came into the kitchen twice while I was resting my eyes before dinner to ask where his snow boots were. See you Tuesday, and thanks.

Something funny after dinner tonight. I sat down on the sofa and Leo marched over and asked me flat out if I was regular tired or doctor tired. When I told him regular tired, he actually let me keep my eyes closed for ten whole minutes.

I closed my eyes on the couch after dinner, waiting for him to drop his Legos or poke me awake like he has every night since December. Instead he pulled the throw blanket over my legs, left his little red hardware-store flashlight on the coffee table, and went to build in his room. First twenty-minute nap I've had in two months.
Leo is here, hon. His mother just kissed the top of his hat and went back out to the car. He's at the fish tank asking if the snail is stuck or asleep. Come on through when you're ready.
Your notes from his first week are in your tote, if you want a look before you go through to the waiting room.
